issue.title: Consolidate per-source PV grain/totals validators into usvote/pv/
issue.body:
**Source:** #36 (PR #81) code review — reuse finding, deferred rather than folded into a UCSB PR.

### What

Two small PV validators are now implemented per source:

- **grain** — `usvote.ucsb.transform.assert_pv_grain` vs. `usvote.mit.transform.assert_unique_grain` (both assert one row per `(year, state, candidate)`)
- **totals-not-exceeded** — `usvote.ucsb.transform.assert_totals_not_exceeded` vs. `usvote.mit.transform.assert_totals_not_exceeded` (logically identical; differ only in error class + message)

They can't be shared by importing one source from the other — sibling PV sources must not couple (the rule that correctly moved the roster contract into `usvote/pv/status.py` and the D018 shape guard into `usvote/pv/schema.py`). So the only correct shared home is `usvote/pv/`.

### Why it's deferred, not done in #36

- It's **DRY-only** — no correctness impact. Each source's transform validates its own frame independently, and the checks agree.
- Doing it in the #36 UCSB PR would pull MIT code into a UCSB change for no behavioural benefit.
- The **shape guard was already consolidated** in #36: `pv.schema.assert_pv_shape` gained an `error_cls` param and UCSB now delegates to it (the one duplicate that had a real drift-caused gap — a dropped `candidate` non-null check).

### Why it's worth doing

The finding predicts a **third consumer**: E6 (#68/#70) unions and compares MIT + UCSB and will want the same grain/totals checks. Consolidating before that lands avoids a third copy.

### Suggested shape

Move both into `usvote/pv/` (alongside `assert_pv_shape` / the roster asserts), each taking `error_cls` (mirroring the established `assert_unique_grain` / `assert_pv_shape` pattern), and have MIT + UCSB both call them. Natural to pick up alongside the E6 shared-surface work (#68).

#373: the replicate ends unmerged at its first in-acceptance stop. The 0.6.0 engine writes nothing that tells step 11's routine merge-gate stop from a step-10 escalation, so no reply is sent and the final message is not classified; the stop's kind is judged afterwards from the stream.

model_tiers: — (every role inherits), as the fixture's loop.config.md binds it: the MODEL_TIERS row is absent
builtin_agents_why: Built-ins spawned with no model/effort run on the parent's stratum: confirmed 2026-11-17 by two sandboxed spikes on CLI 2.1.326 (claude-sonnet-5-5 at medium: Explore, general-purpose and Plan; at high: those three and claude), every record at the parent's (model, effort). Any other built-in (statusline-setup, or claude-code-guide, which runs on its own default) fails check_strata by default-deny.
ci_status_binding: The binding itself is read from repo/.claude/loop.config.md at load time and refused unless it is the Actions-API form (#366). gh run list --workflow ci.yml (Actions API), not the source's gh pr checks: the sandbox gh-token is a fine-grained PAT and cannot read checks (pilot m1, 2026-11-17).

rebinds.why: Every fixture rebinds it to the fixture's label (benchmark-fixture-set.md, rebinds).
The source's gh pr checks is refused by the harness: the sandbox token cannot read checks, so the row reads the Actions API for ci.yml.
The source binds /code-review; the row is the 0.6.0 inline finder fan-out, worded as the pilot's, so every fixture runs the same reviewer. The historical run used /review 115, not the bound skill.
The ledger moves out of .claude/ to .loop-ledger/, as the pilot's: headless writes under .claude/ are refused.
Added: the 0.6.0 engine reads it, and an absent row on a code row that changes a test is a gate-error. The form is the vote repo's own later binding plus --offline.
The 0.0.1 file named a host path to the 0.0.1 engine; it now names ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.
Appends .loop-ledger/, the rebound LEDGER_ROOT, so the ledger stays out of the replicate's tree.
